The HUD after step 3: a deep UX review

Glyph · 2026-10-16 · for Aster, Sky and Latch. Sky's verdict: "this is actually quite good, but it's way too overlay heavy." Notes: panels should collapse; cones are ugly lines and should be a Scout's skill; no constant overlay at the cursor; "meaningless stats" in the History. Read from the code in unity/Assets/Suborned/Runtime/Play/ (HudToolkit, HudModel, PlayHud, HostFeed, HostViews, HostHints, HostActivity, HostFight, HandoverHost) and Sky's three screenshots. Fable reviews the wording in parallel (messages.html); copy appears here only where it is a UX problem. No code, GDD or commit was touched.

0 · The short version

The kit is fine; the screen is noisy because every event is told in many places, and the extras follow the cursor and sit on the agents. Pixel coverage is not the cause: by the layout rectangles the HUD takes 12 to 15 per cent of the screen. The cause is what lands on the street, in the player's eye line: a 14-word tooltip that trails the mouse, two 9-word salmon plates over the downed, number plates under every agent, a progress ring over every busy agent, and cones that are always on. Those come from the IMGUI layer (PlayHud, "step 4") and the always-on world signals (HostViews), not from the kit.

  1. Bug, the "meaningless stats". The seven "Cell" rows are ghost cards: every time both mouse buttons go down in one frame the host sends a panic order, the engine refuses it ("only once a fight is on"), and the refusal is spoken as a scene by a speaker called "cell". The History row then draws only a title, a place and a footer, never the card's lines, so the row is empty. The left tick is a fallback icon, the right pill is a per-row acknowledge button. Section 4.
  2. Cursor. Every hover over a person, a thing or bare ground prices an order (a ~500 KB preview, or an A* five times a second) and paints a chip at the pointer. Sky is right that this is constant. Proposed: hover is a ring and a cursor shape only; the price anchors over the target after a 0.6 s hold, or at once when a verb is armed or a weapon drawn. Section 3.3.
  3. Cones. Three always-on triangle outlines of the full reach, 0.14 m wide, drawn through walls (not clipped by the sight rules the engine uses). Proposed: none by default; the Scout's Watch shows one at a time (the selected or hovered watcher), as a flat filled fan clipped by what blocks sight; Alt shows everything learned. Needs Sky's approval and Keel for the full version. Section 3.4.
  4. Panels. Intel already collapses; the Scenes feed, hint, objective and strips do not. Section 3.2 and the sheet.
  5. Red-family surfaces. The salmon plates are IMGUI "refused" plates (#6B2924-ish at 95 per cent): a near-cone-red surface and a different typeface from the kit. A rule break (§10: red is for small display pictograms and cones) as well as an eyesore.

3 · Rules for a calm screen

3.1 · Six rules

  1. One fact, one place. State of an agent lives on the portrait and its strip. A result lives in the feed. A refusal is one pill at the point of the click. A price is a chip or the panel. Danger is the Alert lamp and the signals in the world. If a fact has a home, nothing else repeats it (Section 2.1).
  2. Three layers. Always: pill, roster, verb plate, and two collapsed pills (Intel, Scenes). Contextual: appears because of what you are doing: the selected agent's ring, strip, badge and route; the hover ring; the armed verb's chip. On demand: a 0.6 s hold, a key, or a skill: price chips, cones, cast icons, numbers, hints, the History.
  3. The street is for the street. Nothing trails the cursor. Nothing with a sentence in it sits on the ground except a refusal, for 2.5 s. Text anchors to what it is about, never to the pointer.
  4. Skills own knowledge. A thing the cell has to find out (who watches where, what a person wants) is not on screen until the Scout has found it out, and then it shows when asked. That is also the pillar "knowing more makes a person cheaper", applied to places.
  5. Never ask the player to dismiss. A notification either asks for a decision (the Alert lamp, a downed agent) or it expires into the History and counts as read. No ✓ chores. (Sky asked for an acknowledge in round 6b; I propose it becomes optional. Flagged for his decision.)
  6. Signals are signals. Cone red, guard amber, rivals violet, only for those, flat and unlit with a shape or motion cue. Nothing else in a red, amber or violet surface: not the refusal plates, not the hint ring, not a hostile's pip plate. A refusal is a teal plate with the small slashed-circle pictogram (the display exception).

How: a click on the header, a hotkey, and a remembered state per panel (PlayerPrefs, as hints already are). The collapsed form is a 30 px pill with a count; a new item shows a dot, never a number that nags.

3.3 · The cursor and the price

Today's rule (§10, and my §14 hold) is "the price chip at the cursor on hover, the run price on ground hover". Sky's note 3 says the cursor must be quiet. Proposed:

Why this is safe for price-before-commit: the action panel and the armed chip are unchanged, and a player who wants prices always can have them by arming a verb or by a settings switch "Prices on hover: always / hold / armed only" (default hold). Side effect: the preview (~500 KB a call) and the move quote (an A* five times a second) run on a hold, not on every mouse move.

On Sky's example line: "7 people near" and "unseen by security" are facts that change no decision, or that the cell may not yet know. The run is the only decision, so the run price shows who will see it only when that is known (the Scout's work), and the people-near count is dropped. This agrees with Fable's cut.

3.4 · Cones become the Scout's Watch

What is drawn now: HostViews.Cone sets a three-point closed LineRenderer from the engine's reach and half-width, 0.14 m wide (a hairline at the play zoom), for every camera, the guard and, when drawn, the rivals, from the first tick. It is not clipped by the roofs, walls and parked vehicles that the engine's sight test honours (§05 "blocked by roofs/parked vehicles"), so it draws what the engine does not test. It is the one thing on screen that the fiction says the cell must work for.

Rule, in two stages.

  1. Stage 1, host only (S–M; no engine change). No cone by default. A cone shows for the selected or hovered watcher (one at a time) when an agent has a clear line to it within 18 m; Alt shows every cone the cell has seen. "Has seen" is derived from positions the engine already has (like CellSees), so a replay is identical.
  2. Stage 2, the Scout's skill (L; Keel and Motive). Watch gains watchers as targets (a camera, the patrol, the guard's post): a timed Watch learns its sight. Learned cones are the ones Alt shows; the one being watched is drawn live and bright. The run chip's "seen by" reads "?" until the sight is learned, exactly like the temperament outcome. An agent who walks into an unknown cone is found out; the warning card is the lesson.

How it is drawn. A flat filled fan at 30 per cent with a crisp 2 px rim: one fill, no gradient (a gradient reads as soft zone edges; Aster's research note says the Shadow Tactics and Desperados III cones keep edges sharp for that reason). The fan is the engine's own test: n rays inside the half angle, each stopped by the first thing that blocks sight, so the shape is notched by hedges, carts and walls. Built at 10 Hz from a read-only Game.ConeFan(source) that Keel would add; drawn unlit, emissive, outside the post grade (§10). One shape cue each, plus a motion cue for the camera: camera a dashed far edge and a scan edge with two fading ghosts; guard chevrons marching the way he faces; rivals diamond ticks. A looped camera goes grey and hatched. One cone at a time keeps them readable (Shadow Tactics' rule, from Aster's note, which I could not trace to a source myself).

Retire KitRest; PlayHud stays only as the F11 comparison view.

4 · The History bug: why seven rows read "Cell"

4.1 · The chain, in the code

  1. The trigger. HandoverHost.Controls (the "both buttons together" line): (left.wasPressedThisFrame && right.isPressed) || (right.wasPressedThisFrame && left.isPressed) calls Panic(p). Any frame where one button goes down while the other is held counts: a drag-select that ends with a right click, a trackpad press with a thumb resting, a fast left–right. Five at 0:26 and two at 0:24 are seven such presses.
  2. The order. Panic sends Order { Op = "cell", Do = "panic" }. Before a fight is on the engine refuses it ("Panic works only once a fight is on", lock code panic-no-fight).
  3. The ghost speaker. HandoverHost.Issue ends a refusal with if (!r.ok && !quietRefusal && o.Do != "move") Say(o.Op, Humanise(o, r), Refused). o.Op is "cell". Say adds a talk line and calls FeedSay("cell", text).
  4. The card. HostFeed.FeedSay: "cell" is not an agent key, there is no open act card, the speaker is not empty, and no event card of this tick exists, so it makes NewCard("city", Text.Speaker("cell"), "·", "", …). PlayText.Speaker has no "cell" entry and capitalises the id: the title is "Cell". The refusal sentence goes into Lines, with no Footer and no Where. It is unread, so it counts in "7 new".
  5. The empty row. HudToolkit.Step3Frame draws a History row from the card's title, place, clock and card.Footer only. The card's Lines are never drawn there. A card with lines and no footer is an empty row. This is general: the same happens for every FeedSay card (a passer-by, a patrol, a watcher): their History rows are bare too.
  6. The left tick. The row's icon is HudModel.AtlasIcon(card.Verb, card.Verb, ""). For a card with no verb it falls through to the default branch, "s_ready", the agent-ready check. It means nothing; the row's own kind should choose the icon.
  7. The right pill. It is the per-card acknowledge button (btn_ack, a "✓" keycap), shown while the card is unread. It moves the card from the stack to the acknowledged list. In the History the list is already the "seen" list, so the pill duplicates "Read all" and the K key.

4.2 · What to do

  • Fix the cause (S). Route a refusal of a cell order (Op == "cell") to the pop only, or to the Fixer as speaker, and never open a city card for a speaker with no entry in names.speakers. Also: a cancelled walk ("Cancelled · Scout / the walk") is not a scene; the pop is enough.
  • Fix the row (S). Show the footer, else the first line as "Name: text". Pick the icon from the card's kind. Remove the per-row pill; unread is a turquoise dot and bold; closing the list marks all read. Give the frame 28 px of side padding: the "S" of SCENES sits under the frame's corner screw and "Read all" under the other.
  • Fix the labels (S). The filter "Cell" collides with the title "Cell"; rename it for what it is, the cell's chatter ("Chatter"). Fable owns the word.

6.1 · Smaller bugs found on the way (not in the ten)

  • HudModel.Frame: the strip hint "Down: select another agent and right click to carry" is clipped by a 170 px ellipsis box. Moot once the strip is compact.
  • The move chip is 568 reference px wide because the s-chip_price sprite is stretched round a sentence; its tail points at nothing. Moot after #3.
  • Marks stack when agents stand together (carrying, lifting): "2 ✓" is printed over "2". Moot after #5.
  • Glyph("carry") returns the word "lift" and Glyph("enter") "in": words, not icons, in the roster and the ring. Map them to s_carrying and enter.
  • OrderTaken says the run-seen line three ways (toast, talk log, and the engine event's warning card). One.
  • The going-loud card is built on the press and the hold is 0.5 s: nobody reads six rows in that time. Show it at the aim.
  • HudToolkit history: ellipsis on a one-line result cuts "Secret: she…". Wrap to two lines.

7 · Proposed GDD changes (for Sky; I have not edited the GDD)

  1. §10 price before commit. Replace "the price chip at the cursor on hover · … the run price on ground hover" with: the price chip anchors over the target after a 0.6 s hold, or at once when a verb is armed or a weapon drawn; the run price shows at the destination flag while the left button is held on the ground; the action panel and the going-loud card as before; "who will see" is shown only for what the Scout has learned. Same in §14's Glyph hold.
  2. §10 HUD list. It names roster, verb plate, pill, chip, two icons and the panel. The build also has Intel, the objective line, the ticker, the slot strips, the scene feed and the hint, all from rounds 6 and 6b and none in the GDD. Add them with the collapse rules in 3.2, and a budget: ≤ 5 % of the screen calm, ≤ 4 words over the street.
  3. §10 readability, §05 security, §03 Scout. "cameras: fixed visible cones" becomes: a cone is drawn for the selected or hovered watcher once the cell has seen it; the Scout's Watch learns a watcher's sight. The fan is the engine's sight test, one at a time, flat, unlit, with its shape or motion cue.
  4. §10 controls. Add Alt (Option) = peek; I = Intel; the hold-to-price and press-hold-to-route behaviours.
  5. §10 feed. Acknowledge becomes optional (auto-read). Sky decides, because he asked for it.
